_comment: What we know about each installed world beyond its own manifest. 'repos' names an upstream that publishes the world file itself - still only accepted if it actually ships an asset matching the world's filename, so a wrong entry is ignored rather than trusted. 'anchors' records a version the world states about something other than itself: the engine it bundles or pins. An anchor is a comparable identifier, NOT the world's own version - two different builds can share one - so the hash in the lock remains the only exact identity. 'no_upstream' records a world confirmed to publish no world file on GitHub, so it reports as checked rather than unexamined. 'clients' records what a player installs to PLAY, which is a different question from where the world file comes from: a slug is absent when nobody has investigated it, which is deliberately distinguishable from state 'none'. The 'bundled' state is never stored here - it is derived from whether the installed apworld ships client.py, so it cannot go stale. Every entry carries the evidence it was read from, so a wrong one can be checked rather than trusted.

pseudoregalia.name: Pseudoregalia Archipelago mod
pseudoregalia.evidence: the world's own docs link this repo's latest release for both the mod and the apworld
pseudoregalia.note: same repo publishes the world file - one download covers both

subnautica.name: Subnautica Archipelago mod
subnautica.evidence: the world's docs name this releases page as where the mod comes from

outer_wilds.name: Outer Wilds Archipelago Randomizer
outer_wilds.note: normally installed through the Outer Wilds Mod Manager rather than by hand

kh2.name: KH2 Panacea / Mod Loader setup
kh2.evidence: the world's docs send players to this guide for the required mod loader
kh2.note: the AP client itself (ArchipelagoKH2Client) ships with Archipelago; this guide covers the game-side setup

ff6wc.name: Worlds Collide
ff6wc.evidence: ff6wc/WorldsCollide/version.py __version__, echoed in __init__.py, Options.py and the docs
ff6wc.note: FF6WC IS Worlds Collide wrapped for Archipelago, not a world that depends on it - the randomizer ships inside at ff6wc/WorldsCollide/. So 1.4.2 is the working version of the game that player is playing, and the closest thing this world has to a version of its own. The apworld still declares none, so the hash remains exact identity.

sm_map_rando.name: Map Randomizer (pysmmaprando)
sm_map_rando.note: that repo publishes the engine wheels, not the world file; the pin is its newest release

look_outside.name: LOArchipelagoPlugins
look_outside.evidence: downloaded from that release; manifest carries no world_version
look_outside.note: version known by where it came from, not by self-declaration

oribf.name: Ori and the Blind Forest world
oribf.evidence: the lobby served it under this version; manifest carries no world_version

dkc.name: Donkey Kong Country world
dkc.evidence: self-declared 1.2.3; the lobby labels its own repack 1.2.3+hotfix1, differing only in Client.py

no_upstream.dkc: distributed via Discord; the lobby serves a 1.2.3+hotfix1 repack
no_upstream.sm_map_rando: no world file published on GitHub; its engine is, see anchors
no_upstream.ff6wc: supplied by the player running it; no public release found
